title: The Opera Game
line: Morphy against the Duke of Brunswick and Count Isouard, Paris 1858: development wins.

steps.text: Paris, 1858. Morphy has three pieces out and aims at two pawns. Black has moved pawns and its queen, and its king is in the middle.
Bring out your last minor piece: the bishop pins the knight to the queen.
steps.after: Black pushes a pawn to chase your bishop on c4.

steps.text: Give the knight for that pawn. It opens lines at Black's king while Black's pieces still sit at home.
Take back with the bishop, with check.
steps.after: A knight blocks the check, and it is pinned.

steps.text: Castle on the long side. Your king gets safe and your rook lands on the open file in one move.
steps.after: Black adds a rook to guard the knight.

steps.text: Take the pinned knight with the rook.
Bring your other rook to the open file. It attacks the pinned rook again.
steps.after: Black's queen steps out of the pin on its knight and offers a trade.

steps.text: Take the rook with your bishop, with check.
steps.after: The knight takes back. Now it alone guards b8.

steps.text: Give your queen with check. The knight must take her.
steps.after: The knight had to leave d7, and the file is open for your rook.
Checkmate. The bishop guards the rook. Black's rook on h8 and bishop on f8 never moved.

summary: Every move brought a white piece into play while Black's pieces stayed home. Develop first.
